message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways, 25 mph in school zones.
• “No‑limit” roads (e.g., I‑10 in some counties) still have a maximum of 75 mph. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster.
• The “no‑seat‑belt” law applies to all vehicles. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited (except for emergency calls).
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Texas Transportation Code §545.002 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02 % BAC).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.
• At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has the right‑of‑way.
• Stop signs and traffic signals must be obeyed. | Texas Transportation Code §545.003 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• No passing a stopped school bus with flashing red lights. | Texas Transportation Code §545.004 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals at least 100 ft before changing lanes.
• Overtaking is allowed only if safe and legal. | Texas Transportation Code §545.005 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces (unless you have a permit), or on sidewalks.
• Parking meters and municipal parking rules apply. | Local city ordinances; Texas Transportation Code §545.006 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing is allowed only for vehicles that are unsafe or obstructing traffic.
• The towing company must notify the owner. | Texas Transportation Code §545.007 | | **Traffic Cameras & Automated Enforcement** | • Cameras enforce speed limits, red‑light violations, and other infractions. | TxDOT and local law‑enforcement agencies | | **Emergency Vehicle Exemptions** | • Police, fire, ambulance, and other emergency vehicles may exceed speed limits and ignore stop signs when responding to emergencies. | Texas Transportation Code §545.008 | ### How to Stay Updated - **TxDOT Website** – Official updates on road conditions, speed limits, and construction projects. - **TxDMV** – Registration, licensing, and inspection requirements. - **Local County Clerk’s Office** – Municipal ordinances and parking regulations. - **Texas Transportation Code** – Full legal text (available online or in print). ### Quick Tips 1. **Always obey posted signs** – they are the law. 2. **Use hands‑free** if you need to talk on the phone. 3. **Check your BAC** before driving; the safest option is to avoid alcohol entirely. 4. **Keep your vehicle in good condition** – regular inspections help avoid penalties. 5. **Know your local rules** – city ordinances can differ from state law (e.g., parking restrictions). Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to handle a particular situation!
